Large pre-trained language models have been shown to store factual knowledge in their parameters.
Large pre-trained language models have been shown to achieve state-of-the-art results when fine-tuned on downstream NLP tasks.
The ability of large pre-trained language models to access and precisely manipulate knowledge is still limited.
The performance of large pre-trained language models on knowledge-intensive tasks lags behind task-specific architectures.
Providing provenance for the decisions of large pre-trained language models and updating their world knowledge remain open research problems.
Pre-trained models with a differentiable access mechanism to explicit non-parametric memory have been investigated only for extractive downstream tasks.
We explore a general-purpose fine-tuning recipe for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) — models which combine pre-trained parametric and non-parametric memory for language generation.
The parametric memory of RAG models is a pre-trained seq2seq model.
The non-parametric memory of RAG models is a dense vector index of Wikipedia.
The non-parametric memory of RAG models is accessed with a pre-trained neural retriever.
We compare two RAG formulations.
One RAG formulation conditions on the same retrieved passages across the whole generated sequence.
Another RAG formulation can use different passages per token.
